items.headline: Moody's spared France: Aa3 affirmed, outlook stays negative — defying the widely expected one-notch cut to A1; wants a deficit-cutting 2027 budget, sees debt >120% of GDP in 2027; S&P reviews France Nov 27 (Le Monde/Reuters, Oct 23)

Brent settled $116.72 (+3.1% Friday, +6.2% week — highest close since April 29); WTI $103.27 (+3.8%, 22-week high) — Houthi attacks on Saudi energy assets + Iran tanker strikes (marketbriefer/WSJ, Oct 23)
Trump at Florida rally: US may do 'another little Epic Fury' against Iran; envoy Barrack: weekend strike 'absolutely' possible; US withdrew some diplomatic staff/relatives from Saudi Arabia (Oct 23)
DXY 101.81 (+0.2% Friday); 10Y 5.00% (+4bp), 2Y 4.69%, 30Y 5.33% — yields reversed part of Thursday's haven rally on hot PMIs + oil (marketbriefer/el-fondo, Oct 23)
Gold closed $3,995.81 (-0.7% Friday, -4.1% week) — first close below $4,000 since July; failed to rally on the risk-off tape as Treasuries/yen/franc took the haven bid (marketbriefer/ING, Oct 23)

USD/CAD 1.40026 (7th straight daily loonie gain) — dipped to 1.39684 intraday before closing back above 1.40; WSJ/Reuters tariff-removal story unconfirmed (White House: speculation) (forexcommand/el-fondo, Oct 23)

New CFTC (week ended Oct 20): hedge funds cut yen shorts, added AUD longs; euro net short largest since March 2020 (94,138 contracts); CAD net short largest since early August; dollar longs <$40B (TradingView/Sina, Oct 23)
ING: the dollar has 'lost its safe-haven status' on AI-crisis vulnerability — tech selloffs only a temporary dollar correction unless stress spreads to credit (el-fondo, Oct 23)
Week ahead: triple-decision Wednesday — RBNZ 8pm CT Tue (~85-89% to 3.00%), BoC 8:45am CT (~75-80%; TD dissents), FOMC 1pm CT (hold ~91-93%; Dec >80%); ECB Thu 8:15am CT; BoJ Fri (newsquawk, Oct 23)

AU Q3 CPI Wednesday the pivot: trimmed +1.0% q/q consensus (~3.5% y/y), headline ~4.0% y/y; Hauser 'materially worse'; GS now expects a November RBA hike; ~50/50 Nov, ~64% Dec (newsquawk/Reuters, Oct 23)

US Q3 GDP advance Thursday: consensus 3.0% SAAR (prev 2.2%), GDPNow 3.5%, Continuum 2.8%; Sep PCE with it — headline +0.5% m/m exp (largest since March), core +0.3% m/m (newsquawk/tradingeconomics, Oct 23)
ECB Thursday: no hike expected; presser to be dominated by OATs/TPI and whether France alters the policy approach; growing chatter about Lagarde's departure (newsquawk, Oct 23)
UK Autumn Budget Wednesday: Healey's first — CGT rise off the table, banks face £2-5B tax rise, headroom £23.6B→~£15B, issuance +~£3B away from the long end (newsquawk, Oct 23)

Houthi claims of attacks on Saudi Yanbu port, an oil field and an airport; Iran stepped up Hormuz tanker attacks (7 struck/mined per IRIB); 30 merchant-ship incidents this month (Bloomberg/marketbriefer, Oct 23)
AUD/USD 0.7036 (+0.2% Friday, above each of the prior ten closes); NZD/USD 0.5700 (+0.3%) — Antipodeans held on the hike repricing into Wednesday's double event (forexcommand, Oct 23)
TD Securities dissents on BoC: hold at 2.25% in October, +25bp Dec and +25bp Jan — vs ~75-80% market pricing for an Oct-28 hike (FXStreet, Oct 23)
UK flash PMIs beat: comp 53.1 (vs 51.8 fcst, strongest since Feb) vs Sep retail sales -0.4% m/m miss (vs -0.1% fcst; Aug rev. up to +0.7%)
Eurozone growth slows to a 4-month low: Oct flash comp 51.9 (vs 52.7 fcst) — France back in contraction (48.9) amid political turmoil, rising energy-driven input costs

Yen shines as AI jitters spur safe-haven rush: USD/JPY ~156.28 (yen's strongest in 1+ months), DXY 101.52, 10Y 4.953% — Nasdaq -2.6% (worst since June) on AI-capex doubts (Meta -7%, AMD -8%, Nvidia -4%); no dollar haven bid
Japan Sep core CPI 2.1% y/y inline — first print above BoJ's 2% target in nine months; core-core 2.4% (from 1.9%), services 1.5% (from 1.2%) — cements the near-term (December ~80%) hike case
AU flash PMIs a big miss: composite 47.7, services 47.8, manufacturing 49.7 (first private-sector contraction in 5 months); input-cost inflation fastest since May
